title: Keep public-profile analytics disabled until rollout is approved
description:
## Context
Public profile actions could instantiate the production analytics transport by default even though production emission is intentionally disabled until ingestion, consent, ownership, idempotency, limits, and retention receive separate approval. The final parity audit changes the default provider transport to the disabled adapter while preserving explicitly injected test transports.

## User story
As a profile owner and visitor, I need public-profile actions to remain privacy-safe during the parity rollout so no production analytics are emitted before the rollout contract is approved.

## Acceptance criteria
- A public profile rendered with the default AnalyticsProvider does not send production analytics.
- An explicitly injected controlled transport still receives valid descriptors in tests.
- The existing production endpoint is not enabled or broadened by this fix.
- Focused analytics tests, typecheck, lint, and the final parity verification pass.

## References
- Branch: codex/public-profile-parity-final-audit
- Fixing commit: 2f2f1925
- Final pull request: pending
- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Keep review changes and external review collections complete after reload
description:
## Context
Review manager failures could leave mutation state inconsistent, rejected operations were not uniformly retained for retry, seven public templates reduced external review pages to one link, and the completed external-review collection lacked an owner-managed visible section title. The final parity audit hardens mutation failure handling, preserves complete ordered collections, and gives owners one safe heading that is projected to every public template without invented template copy.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need review edits, every saved external review page, and my chosen section title to persist in their intended order so the public bio matches the dashboard after reload.

## Acceptance criteria
- Review and external-page create, update, visibility, reorder, and delete reload the preview exactly once after authoritative success and zero times after returned or thrown failure.
- Failed operations retain a usable retry state and do not leave controls permanently busy.
- Public templates render every valid enabled external review page in deterministic rank-and-ID order.
- The dashboard accepts a normalized optional external-review section title and retains its draft on failure.
- All nine templates display the owner-authored title when configured, use no hardcoded public fallback heading, and keep blank-title links accessible.
- The private dentistry value synchronizes through the read-only public_profiles projection; the owner/admin RPC and generated types preserve that boundary.
- Focused manager, action, query, component, database-boundary, pgTAP, and dashboard/public reload coverage pass.

## References
- Branch: codex/public-profile-parity-final-audit
- Fixing commits: 2f2f1925, 5fa2c24c, 0161f7f0
- Boundary/type evidence: 6d3f35af, 9440b805, 6f13b42c
- Final pull request: pending
- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Refresh the dashboard preview after treatment and service changes
description:
## Context
Successful treatment and service item mutations updated saved data but did not reliably refresh the public-bio preview, making the editor appear to do nothing. The remediation gives create, update, delete, and reorder the same success-only preview refresh contract for both item kinds.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need the dashboard preview to reflect every successful treatment or service change immediately so I can trust what will appear on my public bio.

## Acceptance criteria
- Treatment and service create, update, delete, and reorder each refresh the preview exactly once after authoritative success.
- Returned failures and rejected mutations refresh the preview zero times.
- Both treatment and service paths have focused wrapper coverage.
- Dashboard Playwright instrumentation verifies exact iframe refresh counts without relying on unrelated load events.

## References

- Fixing commit: 6c99e033
- Final pull request: pending
- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Keep safe HTTP links visible and reject credential-bearing links
description:
## Context
The dashboard accepted ordinary HTTP links but the public profile silently omitted them, while credential-bearing authority URLs needed an explicit safety boundary. The remediation aligns dashboard and public parsing around credential-free HTTP(S) URLs.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need every safe link accepted by the dashboard to appear on my public bio while unsafe credential-bearing URLs are rejected consistently.

## Acceptance criteria
- Credential-free HTTP and HTTPS links accepted by the dashboard remain visible on every applicable public template.
- URLs containing username or password authority credentials are rejected at the dashboard boundary and excluded publicly.
- Native anchor behavior and controlled link analytics descriptors remain intact.
- Seven-template fixtures, exact verifiers, unit tests, and public Playwright sentinels pass.

## References
- Branch: codex/public-profile-parity-final-audit
- Fixing commit: 6c99e033
- Final pull request: pending
- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Keep blog inventories deterministic, null-safe, and owner-authored
description:
## Context
Equal-rank blog groups and posts could render in nondeterministic order, malformed or null embedded relations could crash Cosmetic and Expert templates, and Specialist added unmanaged static blog headings instead of using owner-authored group names. The remediation centralizes rank-and-ID ordering, validates embedded relations, and removes unmanaged Specialist copy.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need every saved blog to render in stable order using my authored section names without crashes or invented template copy.

## Acceptance criteria
- The public query and all eight template selectors order blog groups and posts by rank then stable ID.
- Null embedded groups or posts do not crash public rendering.
- Duplicate or mismatched embedded relations are rejected rather than silently misclassified.
- Specialist uses the owner-authored blog group name as its section heading and adds no unmanaged static heading.
- Focused selector, query, static-copy, and Playwright contract tests pass.

## References

- Fixing commit: 6c99e033
- Final pull request: pending
- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Give Clinic before-and-after gallery media unique analytics positions
description:
## Context
Clinic and Commerce before-and-after controls reported the same visible position for both images in a comparison, making conversion analytics unable to distinguish which media the visitor opened. The remediation assigns a unique one-based visible position to every before, after, and general-gallery item.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need gallery analytics to distinguish each visible image so engagement reports reflect the media visitors actually open.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each before image reports position 2n-1 and each paired after image reports position 2n.
- General-gallery positions begin after all comparison images.
- Native button and accessible lightbox behavior remain unchanged.
- Controlled analytics descriptor tests prove every visible media position is unique and one-based.

- Fixing commit: 210c698c

- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Use real owner-scoped location media in Batch C showcases
description:
## Context
Clinic, Specialist, and Trust Batch C showcases reused unrelated preview or general-gallery images as location media, so location parity evidence did not prove real owner-scoped saved objects. The remediation adds nine valid WebP fixtures in the expected owner, dentistry, and location namespaces with exact informative or decorative alt policy.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need every saved location to display its own valid image so the public bio represents the actual location rather than unrelated gallery content.

## Acceptance criteria
- Clinic, Specialist, and Trust showcase locations reference real decodable WebP objects in their exact owner/dentistry/location namespaces.
- Seed and verifier checks prove exact paths, ordering, and alt/decorative behavior.
- Desktop and mobile public tests prove images load with nonzero naturalWidth before and after reload.
- Existing accessibility scans continue to pass.
